name: crew
description: Makes the main session a lead that delegates to six specialist subagents: code-reader and research on Haiku; designer, developer and tester on Sonnet; architect on Opus. With the jevKey option set (a TypeSafe key), Jev may move each call's model one step (the architect stays on Opus) and raise its effort to high; that sends a redacted, truncated prompt to api.typesafe.ai. When a local HTTP loopback proxy is ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, each role also gets a fixed-model crew:<role>-codex twin. Calls may be routed automatically to those twins when Codex has more weekly headroom, with or without Jev; what those subagents read and write goes to OpenAI through the proxy.

jevKey.title: Jev API key (TypeSafe)
jevKey.description: Setting this key turns Jev routing on; leaving it empty turns it off. With a key, Jev (TypeSafe) chooses the model and effort of each crew:* Agent call, one step from the agent's default and never below the architect's Opus floor or medium effort, and the choice shows in the task's description. The call's description and its prompt (secrets and paths removed, cut to 4000 characters) are sent to api.typesafe.ai. Only automatic quota routing may move a call to its role's Codex twin, even without this key, and a base-role call that names a model keeps it. The key is sent only in the Authorization header and is never logged or stored by the plugin. A repository's own settings cannot supply it.
